summary: Automated payfile generation failing: vendor beneficiary name encoding causing XML validation errors
description:
Issue summary:
Automated SEPA payfile generation for weekly vendor payouts is failing XML schema validation for a subset of vendors. Failures are traced to beneficiary name fields containing unusual Unicode characters and non-breaking spaces introduced during vendor onboarding imports.

Impact:
- Scheduled payout job for EU vendors is blocked (next window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC).
- ~27 vendor payments (single-entity, low total $) remain in pending state and cannot be exported to bank. Finance team awaiting manual remediation.

Environment:
- Prod payout pipeline (weekly_payrun_v3) running in eu-west region.
- Bank file format: SEPA XML PAIN.001 v001.001.03, schema validation enforced by internal validator before FTP delivery.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run the payfile generation locally with the same vendor dataset (export attached list reproduced in investigation notes).
2) Observe validator failure when beneficiary name element contains U+00A0 (NBSP) or U+2019 (right single quotation) followed by multiple combining marks.
3) Validator reports "InvalidCharInElementContent" at line/column corresponding to <DbtrNm> value.

Observed behavior:
- XML schema validator (internal) rejects file with error referencing invalid characters in text nodes.
- The payfile generation job marks entire batch as failed; no partial export is produced.

Expected behavior:
- Generator should normalize vendor name fields into a bank-acceptable subset (trim non-printing spaces, normalize quotes) and either replace or surface clear validation errors per-vendor so remediation can be targeted.

Notable recent changes:
- Vendor data ingestion pipeline had a one-off migration on 2026-03-02 that preserved original encoding and inserted NBSPs in some name fields.
- Payments validator was upgraded on 2026-03-10 to stricter XML rules to match bank sandbox parsing.

investigation_notes: Validated failing XML against internal validator; error message: 'InvalidCharInElementContent at /Document/CstmrCdtTrfInitn/PmtInf/CreditTransferTransactionInformation/Dbtr/Nm'.

Identified 27 affected vendor rows. Common pattern: names with non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) and smart quotes from legacy CSV imports. Example original value: 'ACMEA0CoE28099s' which becomes invalid in strict XML output.

Temporary fix implemented: normalization pipeline (NFKC) + replace NBSP with regular space + map curved quotes to ASCII. Sanitizer script location: github.com/redwood-inference/payments/commit/af3b9c (PR referenced above).

Risk assessment: Low risk for most vendors, but must keep audit of original value. Bank expects exact name match for some European banks; we need to record both original and sanitized values in payment remittance metadata.

Proposed longer-term changes: 1) Add validation on vendor onboarding + UI warning. 2) Add per-vendor validation report in payfile generator instead of failing whole batch. 3) Add automated revertable transform with audit columns saved to vendor_payments table.
resolution: Workaround applied and payments processed: ran sanitized export that normalized unicode characters and removed NBSPs, then validated and delivered the SEPA file. Finance confirmed 27 vendor payments settled. Next steps: merge PR to add sanitizer into payfile generation pipeline (PR#1284), add onboarding validation (follow-up INT-822469), and implement audit trail for sanitized fields. Logged follow-up task for product to add UI-level warnings for vendor import.
